subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find the equation of the parabola whose vertex is (1, −2), focus is (1, −7).

mark_split.label: Find the direction of the axis and the value of a

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Find the axis direction and a
steps.margin_note: First mark, for the direction of the axis and a = 5.
lines: The x-coordinates of A and S are equal,
so the axis is parallel to the y-axis.
steps.why: Two points with the same x-coordinate lie on a vertical line, so the axis must be parallel to the y-axis; which way the parabola opens follows from which of the two points, vertex or focus, is lower down.
common_mistakes: Comparing the y-coordinates instead of the x-coordinates to decide the axis direction.
Writing a = 25 instead of a = 5 by forgetting to take the square root.
steps.memory_tip: Equal x-coordinates mean a vertical axis; the focus sitting below the vertex means the parabola opens downward.

steps.label: Write the equation
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for the correct equation with the minus sign that marks a downward parabola.
steps.why: Once the direction and a are known, the vertex form (x−h)² = −4a(y−k) is a direct substitution, with the minus sign marking the downward opening.
common_mistakes: Using the upward form (x−h)² = 4a(y−k) here instead of the downward form with the minus sign.
Writing −4a as −20 correctly but then dropping the minus sign in the next line.
steps.memory_tip: Upward parabola: (x−h)² = 4a(y−k). Downward: the same with a minus sign in front of 4a.

insider_note: 126.1 and 126.2 are a deliberate contrast pair — one upward, one downward — printed side by side so the only real difference to notice is the sign in front of 4a.
